title: Enriched extension from adjunction data to the walking coherent adjunction
statement:
Use quasicategories and coherent transformations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], adjunction units, counits and triangle witnesses of [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data], the ordinal conventions of [def-coef-coherent-monad-modules], and compatible enriched simplicial presentations of [lem-coef-enriched-simplicial-presentation]. A locally quasicategorical simplicial category $\mathscr K$ is a simplicial category with every hom-simplicial set a quasicategory. Its homotopy $2$-category has these same objects and hom-categories the homotopy categories of those quasicategories.

Let $L:c\to d$ and $U:d\to c$ be arrows of $\mathscr K$, with unit $\eta:1_c\to UL$, counit $\epsilon:LU\to1_d$ and triangle witnesses presenting an adjunction in its homotopy $2$-category. Let $\mathsf{Adj}$ be the simplicial category obtained by taking the nerve of each hom-category of the free $2$-category on an adjunction $\ell\dashv u$; its endomorphism at the source of $\ell$ is $D=N(\Delta_+)$, and its hom from the target of $\ell$ to that source is $W=N(\Delta_\infty)$, with the left $D$-action by composition. There exists a simplicial functor $H:\mathsf{Adj}\to\mathscr K$ taking $\ell,u,\eta,\epsilon$ to $L,U,\eta,\epsilon$. One chosen triangle witness can also be fixed; no assertion is made that both prescribed witnesses are fixed simultaneously.

Restriction of $H$ gives a strict simplicial walking-monad diagram with endofunctor $UL$, unit $\eta$ and multiplication $U\epsilon L$, and a strictly $D$-equivariant map
$$W\longrightarrow\mathscr K(d,c).$$
The latter has singleton value $U$ and action transformation $U\epsilon:ULU\to U$; all its higher action simplices are restrictions of $H$. When $\mathscr K$ is a compatible enriched presentation, these are enriched transformations and their entire higher simplices. When the adjunction arrows and transformations preserve tensors by specified coherent comparisons, choose the presentation retaining that data: the extension retains it as well. Thus evaluating the displayed equivariant map on objects of $E_d$ gives the coherent action of $UL$ on $UY$ and does so in the full enriched functor category, before taking any homotopy category.

source.place: Theorems 4.3.9 and 4.3.11, and the limitation in Remark 4.3.12; section 6.1 identifies the walking monad and module by restriction. Enriched specialization uses the separately stated compatible presentation. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this extension theorem.

proof.text: Fix the prescribed triangle $\beta$ at $L$, whose successive edges are $L\eta,\epsilon L$ and whose long edge is $1_L$. The freeness clause of [lem-coef-walking-adjunction-cell-filtration] gives a simplicial functor $H_0:A_0\to\mathscr K$ sending the five generators to $L,U,\eta,\epsilon,\beta$. Their boundaries agree by the specified adjunction data. Use the same lemma to fix its filtration $A_i$. The inductive assertion will be: $H_i:A_i\to\mathscr K$ is a simplicial functor restricting to $H_0$ on $A_0$, and each successor restricts to its predecessor.

Given $H_i$, restrict it along each type (i) attaching map in [lem-coef-walking-adjunction-cell-filtration]. A functor from $2[\Lambda_k^n]$ is exactly a horn in the hom-simplicial set between the two chosen object images. This hom is a quasicategory, so its inner horn has a filler by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A filler defines the required functor from $2[\Delta^n]$ agreeing on the horn. This uses only $0<k<n$, never an arbitrary outer-horn filler.

For a type (ii) attachment, its boundary diagram under $H_i$ has $1\to2$ equal to $L$. By the final-edge clause of [lem-coef-walking-adjunction-cell-filtration], the apex is $a=1_d$ or $a=L$, the last $0\to1$ vertex is $Ua$, and the final cone edge is exactly $\epsilon a$. These are equalities of simplices, because $H_i$ is a simplicial functor and already fixes $L,U,\epsilon$. Apply [lem-coef-counit-cone-boundary-extension] with $z=d$ or $z=c$, respectively, to obtain an extension on $3[\Delta^m]$ agreeing with every earlier boundary simplex. Its hypotheses use the given adjunction in the homotopy $2$-category and local quasicategoricality, with $m\geq1$.

source.place: Theorem 4.3.8, second case; Observation 4.3.4 and Proposition 4.3.6

proof.text: For each finite family of attachments, the fillers of the preceding two steps and $H_i$ agree on every gluing domain. The pushout property in [lem-coef-walking-adjunction-cell-filtration] therefore defines $H_{i+1}$ with $H_{i+1}|_{A_i}=H_i$. This proves the inductive assertion, starting from step 1. On the union define $H(\sigma)=H_i(\sigma)$ whenever $\sigma\in A_i$. The restriction equalities make this independent of $i$. Each face, degeneracy or finite composite occurs in some common $A_i$, so its preservation follows there. Since the union is $\mathsf{Adj}$, this constructs the asserted simplicial functor and fixes all the initial generators.

source.place: Proofs of Theorems 4.3.8 and 4.3.11: successive pushouts and their countable union

proof.text: Restrict $H$ to the object $c$ of the walking adjunction. Its hom is $D=N(\Delta_+)$, as specified in the statement. The singleton, the empty-to-singleton map and the two-to-singleton map are respectively $u\ell$, $\eta$ and $u\epsilon\ell$. Their images are $UL$, $\eta$ and $U\epsilon L$. Composition and identities in a simplicial functor are preserved strictly in every degree; consequently ordinal sum and its empty unit act strictly. This is precisely the walking-monad diagram of [def-coef-coherent-monad-modules], with all its higher simplices given by restriction.

source.place: Introduction 1.3 and section 6.1, restriction to Mnd

proof.text: On the hom from $d$ to $c$, set $h=H_{d,c}:W\to\mathscr K(d,c)$. For $v\in D_r$ and $w\in W_r$, simplicial functoriality gives $h(v\cdot w)=H_{c,c}(v)\circ h(w)$; thus $h$ is strictly $D$-equivariant in every degree. The singleton in $W$ is $u$, and the last-element-preserving collapse of the two-element ordinal is the whiskered counit $u\epsilon$. Hence their images are $U$ and $U\epsilon:ULU\to U$. This checks the underlying action and its orientation against [def-coef-coherent-monad-modules]; all higher action and compatibility simplices are the corresponding images under $H$, rather than separately chosen homotopies.

source.place: Sections 3.3.6 and 6.1: restriction of the representable Adj(-,+)

proof.text: For a compatible enriched presentation take $\mathscr K=\mathscr P$ from [lem-coef-enriched-simplicial-presentation]. Its hom-quasicategories identify the whole simplicial sets of enriched functors and transformations, compatibly with composition and evaluation. Apply steps 1--6 inside that presentation. Thus the output simplices live in its enriched transformation homs. Evaluation of $h$ at $Y\in E_d$ sends its singleton to $UY$ and its action edge to $U\epsilon_Y$; degreewise evaluation supplies every higher action simplex as well. If coherent tensor comparisons are part of the input, the tensor-preserving version of the cited presentation retains those comparisons in its hom-quasicategories. Performing the same construction there retains them throughout. Forgetting those comparisons yields the preceding construction. No assertion about enriched coherence is inferred merely from an ordinary homotopy-category equality.

source.place: Enriched specialization of Theorem 4.3.11 using the separately stated compatible presentation

proof.text: The construction fixed $\beta$ because it was already in $A_0$. It imposes no equality with the other prescribed triangle witness: its image is the $2$-simplex subsequently produced when the relevant cell is attached. This is why both initially prescribed witnesses have not been asserted to extend together. If the chosen witness is instead the triangle at $U$, reverse the direction of all $1$-arrows and use the left adjoint $U^{\mathrm{op}}$ with right adjoint $L^{\mathrm{op}}$ in $\mathscr K^{\mathrm{op}}$; the same unit and counit now have the required reversed types. Reversing back the resulting diagram gives the original adjunction and fixes that witness. Reversal preserves each hom-simplicial set and strict composition, so this introduces no additional filling assumption.

source.place: Theorem 4.3.11 and Remark 4.3.12; formal duality for the other choice

proof_origin.place: Agent-written specialization of the cell induction of Riehl--Verity 4.3.8--4.3.11, with restrictions as in 6.1; online source read, archival copy WANTED.
